ai.headline: OpenAI + Plaid: ChatGPT connects to live financial accounts
ai.body: OpenAI is partnering with Plaid to let ChatGPT Pro users connect read-only financial account data for personalised budgeting, debt repayment, and planning guidance. The integration shifts ChatGPT from generic advice to account-specific recommendations — a direct wedge into personal finance workflows. OpenAI explicitly positions it as non-advisory, but the data access surface is significant.

ai.headline: Grab's production multi-agent system: architecture, failure modes, and lessons
ai.body: Grab built a LangGraph + FastAPI multi-agent system to automate data warehouse investigation and schema enhancement requests, freeing engineers from ~2 days/week of support work. Key design choices: separate read-only (four specialised agents + summariser) from write operations (single enhancement agent with mandatory human gates), and use a classifier agent for routing with explicit reasoning trails. Six production failure classes were encountered post-launch, and deliberate feedback loops drove ongoing quality improvement.

ai.headline: Anthropic Mythos Preview benchmarked for offensive security by XBOW
ai.body: XBOW ran Anthropic's Mythos Preview through pentest-style benchmarks and found it sharply reduces false negatives on web exploit discovery and excels at source-code reasoning including firmware and Chromium reverse engineering. Weaknesses remain in live-site validation, edge-case command safety, and cost efficiency — XBOW treats it as one strong engine in a multi-model fleet rather than a universal default.

ai.headline: AI hardware portability is structurally impossible: the kernel divergence case
ai.body: A detailed analysis argues that AI kernel portability across TPU (Pallas), NVIDIA (CuTile/CUTLASS), AWS (NKI), AMD (FlyDSL), and Tenstorrent (tt-Metalium) is impossible because the algorithms themselves diverge per hardware — not just the syntax. Evidence: MaxText MoE grouped matmul is 282 lines of Pallas on TPU; the equivalent for NVIDIA Blackwell SM100 requires 4 million lines of generated CUDA with zero shared code.

ai.headline: Braze CTO: 60%+ of committed code is now AI-generated; inference cost is the new bottleneck
ai.body: Braze achieved AI-first engineering within months, with Claude Code and Opus 4.5 driving adoption via a greenfield MCP server. The emergent problem is inference cost — engineers are spending tens to hundreds of dollars per day on AI usage, surfacing a sustainability question that mirrors the broader enterprise AI subscription pricing risk.

sec.headline: CISA contractor leaked AWS GovCloud admin keys + plaintext passwords on public GitHub for 6 months
sec.body: A Nightwing contractor maintained a public GitHub repo 'Private-CISA' since November 2025 containing admin credentials for three AWS GovCloud accounts, a plaintext password CSV for dozens of internal CISA systems, and the agency's Artifactory package repository credentials — a prime supply-chain pivot point. The contractor had explicitly disabled GitHub's secret-scanning default. Exposed AWS keys remained valid for 48 hours after CISA was notified. CISA says no evidence of compromise, but the artifactory access would allow backdooring every subsequent software build.

sec.headline: node-ipc npm package compromised in supply chain attack — credential exfiltration via DNS TXT
sec.body: A supply chain attack has compromised the widely-used node-ipc npm package with a heavily obfuscated infostealer that exfiltrates credentials using DNS TXT records, a covert channel that bypasses many egress controls. Any project with a direct or transitive dependency on node-ipc should treat the package as untrusted and rotate secrets.

sec.headline: OpenClaw: four chained vulnerabilities enabling host escape, secret leakage, and privilege escalation
sec.body: Cyera Research disclosed four chainable flaws in OpenClaw: a TOCTOU write escape enabling host-level changes, environment variable leakage of secrets, a loopback bug granting owner rights, and a TOCTOU read escape exposing arbitrary files. The chain allows progression from a malicious plugin or prompt injection to data theft and persistent foothold on exposed instances — patch and rotate secrets immediately.

sec.headline: Grafana GitHub token breach: codebase exfiltrated, CoinbaseCartel extortion attempt
sec.body: An attacker used a stolen GitHub token to download Grafana's full codebase and demanded payment; Grafana invalidated credentials, hardened controls, and refused to pay. The incident is attributed to the CoinbaseCartel group, which specialises in data theft and extortion across sectors — a pattern directly relevant to any org with valuable IP in GitHub.

sec.headline: Akamai acquires LayerX for $205M — browser-layer security for SaaS and AI agents
sec.body: Akamai is acquiring Israeli startup LayerX for ~$205M cash, adding browser-layer controls that sit atop standard browsers (no forced enterprise browser swap) and cover SaaS apps, generative AI tools, and AI agent sessions. LayerX already supports AI-focused browsers like Atlas and Comet, positioning Akamai to enforce policy on the fast-growing non-human identity / agentic access surface.

fin.headline: Klarna Q1 2026: $1B revenue (+44% YoY), GMV $33.7B (+33%), operating profit $68M vs $3M prior year
fin.body: Klarna's Q1 results confirm accelerating profitability ahead of its IPO, with adjusted operating profit growing 22x YoY. Growth is driven by wallet coverage expansion across Pay Now, Pay Later, and Fair Financing, and the Walmart partnership via OnePay is performing in line with expectations despite Affirm maintaining residual volume through card usage.

fin.headline: Anthropic Claude for Small Business integrates with QuickBooks, PayPal, HubSpot — threatens vertical fintech incumbents
fin.body: Claude for Small Business plugs directly into QuickBooks, PayPal, HubSpot, and others to run payroll, close the month, and chase invoices — effectively commoditising an entire category of vertical fintech SaaS at no marginal cost. The 'Token Economy' analysis identifies this as a Level 4 AI adoption pattern and warns that companies stuck at Level 1 (personal productivity tools) face acquisition on bad terms or irrelevance.

fin.headline: a16z leads Stitch Series A: API-first core banking OS for Middle East with native KYC/KYB and AI workflows
fin.body: Andreessen Horowitz is investing in Stitch, an API-first core banking operating system covering general ledger, cards, loans, bank accounts, and built-in KYC/KYB workflow integrations. The bet targets the Middle East where greenfield financial institutions need modern infrastructure designed for clean APIs, data access, and AI-native operations from day one.

swe.headline: Claude Code at scale: patterns for monorepos, legacy systems, and microservice sprawl
swe.body: Anthropic's official guidance on Claude Code in production covers organisations with thousands of developers across monorepos (millions of lines), decades-old legacy systems, and distributed microservice repositories. Key patterns address context management, CLAUDE.md configuration, and task decomposition strategies that differ substantially from single-repo usage.

swe.headline: Context pruning: up to 20x token compression with quality preservation for LLM applications
swe.body: Context pruning removes low-value tokens or passages from LLM inputs and can achieve up to 20x compression with faster latency by mitigating 'lost in the middle' degradation in long context windows. The technique requires care with structured data and multi-turn dialogue, where aggressive pruning can degrade output quality.

swe.headline: Enterprise AI subscription pricing: subsidised today, usage-based reckoning incoming
swe.body: Major AI labs are currently pricing enterprise subscriptions below cost to drive workflow lock-in; agentic AI has made the gap between flat fees and actual compute cost worse. Pre-IPO pressure will force a shift to usage-based pricing, and organisations running high-volume agentic workloads face significant cost exposure — Braze's per-engineer daily AI spend is an early data point.

mkt.headline: Andy Jassy's Amazon AI bets: deep profile of five-year tenure and strategic direction
mkt.body: A long-form profile covers Jassy's restructuring of Amazon — cutting projects and staff to satisfy Wall Street — and his current series of expensive AI bets described as audacious even by Silicon Valley standards. Portfolio-relevant as AMZN's strategic trajectory under Jassy differs materially from Bezos-era capital allocation.

mkt.headline: Musk v. Altman jury deliberations begin; OpenAI nonprofit-to-for-profit conversion liability on the line
mkt.body: An advisory jury began deliberations in the federal OpenAI case, with District Judge Gonzalez Rogers holding final authority over whether Altman, Brockman, and OpenAI are liable for unjust enrichment via the nonprofit-to-for-profit conversion. The remedies phase runs concurrently, creating structural uncertainty for OpenAI's commercial trajectory and by extension its enterprise customers and competitors.

deepDives.title: CISA AWS GovCloud Key Leak — Krebs on Security
deepDives.why: Primary reporting on the most significant US government credential exposure in recent memory, directly relevant to cloud IAM hygiene, secret scanning controls, and supply-chain risk via exposed Artifactory credentials.

deepDives.title: Grab Engineering: From Firefighting to Building — Multi-Agent AI Production Case Study
deepDives.why: Detailed engineering post-mortem from a production multi-agent deployment at scale, covering architectural decisions (LangGraph, specialised agents, risk-tiered autonomy), the six failure classes encountered, and the feedback loop design — directly applicable to agentic system design.

deepDives.title: XBOW Evaluation of Anthropic Mythos for Offensive Security
deepDives.why: Primary technical benchmark of a new AI model against real pentest workflows, with honest assessment of strengths (source-code reasoning, firmware RE) and weaknesses (live-site validation, cost) — actionable for teams evaluating AI-assisted vulnerability discovery.
